name: Scrubbed transformation sequence
look: One object goes through one change of state as the page scrolls (raw to finished, closed to open, lifted and handed over), played as a frame sequence on a canvas on the page's own ground: the thing it came from slides away, the thing it ends on rises under it and short labels land beside the finished object. Use it only when there are 80-250 rendered or filmed frames, with alpha, of the object changing.
reduced: The finished composition: the markup as the page writes it, nothing moving.
phone: The same fractions on the phone frame set, the object centred and wider than the screen, the after line in a top slot at about the before statement's size, and the callouts as a stack of up to four plain rows (no bullets) that takes the statement's slot as it lifts away; hold 3. Data-saving visitors get the finished composition and download no frames.
place: In the middle, on the showcase or how it is made, or as the page's finale before the action: the before statement opens it and the after line with one action closes it.
content: A frame sequence of the object changing, about 120 frames (80-250), square with alpha, from a locked-off camera, the object filling most of the frame with its foot in the same place at the end: desktop frames about twice the box's size (1600px), a phone set of every second frame (about 1000px). Optional cut-outs of the before context (what it came from) and the receiver (the plinth, shelf or pad it ends on), rendered by the same cameras. A before statement of 5-7 words (36 characters at most) as the headline, up to six callouts of 2-6 words set beside the last frame's silhouette, with no marker (three is right), an after line of 3-6 words and a 2-3 word action. Never fake it by turning one still: without the footage, redraw.
options: frames, the desktop URL pattern (#### is the zero-padded index; required, else the finished composition); count 120 (2-400; 80-250 for a good scrub); phoneFrames and phoneCount (60 with its own pattern); hold 4 (3-5); phoneHold 3 (2-4); scrub 0.6, 0.3 with Stage.smooth(); split 0.85 (0.5-0.95) share of the frames played evenly; ground 'none' (the page's own ground, the default) | 'iris' (old pages only, never dealt: a drawn disc that becomes a second ground); irisAt [0.5, 0.54] the camera's pivot; push 1.25 (1-1.4) how far the camera starts pushed in; firstBox [0.17, 0.3, 0.83, 0.81] the object's outline in the first frame; centre true, the object glides to the centre while the title is away (laptop). Labels, the statement and the after line land on a clock, never half-way on the scroll.
